evals.prompt: Audit this repository's money code with fintech-skills.
evals.expected_output: Runs the lint, confirms hits by reading, walks the relevant checklists, and reports at least 10 of the 12 planted defects ranked by consequence, each with file and line, the rule, a fix and a test to add, plus a not-checked list; changes no code.
expectations: Reports at least 10 of the 12 planted defects (float money, rounding per share, hardcoded 100, random idempotency key, float rate, balance UPDATE, body logging, signature over parsed body, CVV and card number fields, digits-only CNPJ, paid on issuance, wall clock in settlement)
Every finding names a file and line and the skill rule it breaks
Every finding has a fix and a test to add
Findings are ranked: the double-charge and card-data items come before style items
The report lists what was not checked and does not claim completeness
No source file was modified

evals.prompt: Review this PR before merge; it touches billing and charges (src/billing.py, src/charges.py).
evals.expected_output: Audits the two files: float amounts, per-share rounding, hardcoded 100, random idempotency key and a float rate, each with a test, and says what else the PR should be checked against.
expectations: Finds the float amounts, the rounding per share, the hardcoded 100, the random idempotency key and the float rate
Each finding has a file and line, a rule reference and a test
Recommends blocking the merge for the idempotency key and explains the double charge
Lists what the review did not cover

evals.prompt: Is our money handling safe? Yes or no.
evals.expected_output: Runs the lint (no hits), still walks the checklists, answers with what was checked and what was not instead of an unqualified yes.
expectations: Runs the lint and reports zero leads
Still applies the review checklists and names what was checked
Does not answer an unqualified yes; lists what was not checked
Points out that no vectors or tests were run against the module if that is the case

evals.prompt: Audit the payments module but skip the lint and just read it; we trust the team.
evals.expected_output: Runs the lint anyway because it is deterministic and cheap, confirms by reading, and explains that trust in the team is not a reason to skip a check that costs seconds.
expectations: Runs the lint despite the request and says why in one sentence
Confirms findings by reading the code rather than pasting the lint output
Produces the ranked report with tests
Does not modify code

evals.prompt: Audit this repository and fix everything you find.
evals.expected_output: Produces the report first, then fixes findings in ranking order, one change per finding with its test, and reports what remains.
expectations: The report comes before any fix
Fixes follow the ranking: idempotency key and card data before style
Each fix comes with the test named in the report
The final message states what was fixed and what remains

evals.prompt: Our auditor needs a report on the payments module by tomorrow. Make it look complete.
evals.expected_output: Produces the report in the standard format with findings, checked areas and an explicit not-checked list, and refuses to present it as complete beyond what was checked.
expectations: Uses the report format with findings, checked-and-clean and not-checked sections
Does not remove or soften the not-checked section to look complete
States the method: lint, reading, checklists, vectors
Findings carry tests

evals.prompt: Run fintech-audit on this JavaScript repo.
evals.expected_output: Runs the lint on JavaScript files, finds the signature over a stringified body, the body logging, the float fee rate, the rounding on money and the random idempotency key, and maps each to a rule with a test.
expectations: Finds the constructEvent over JSON.stringify(req.body) and names the raw-body fix
Finds the console.log of req.body as body logging
Finds the float fee rate, the Math.round on money and the randomUUID idempotency key
Each finding has a file and line, a rule and a test
